title: Identification of protease cleavage-sites in E. coli lysate by differential N-terminomic analysis
protocol: Streak out E. coli K12 MG1655 on 2xYT plates and grow overnight at 37°C.
Pick a well-isolated colony into 50 mL of 2xYT medium and grow with shaking at about 225 rpm overnight at 37°C.
Innoculate two 500 mL cultures with 10 mL of the overnight culture. Grow at 37°C with shaking, monitoring the optical density at 600 nm.
Harvest the cultures in an RC 5B centrifuge at 4°C with the SLA-3000 rotor at 5000 rpm for 10 minutes when the OD600 equals 1.0.
Decant the media and scrape the pellets into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 30 mL of ice cold buffer (e.g., 50 mM HEPES with 10% sucrose) to the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet by vortexing.
Sonicate with a large probe at 50% intensity and duty cycle for 2 minutes, keeping bacteria on ice.
Transfer sonicated bacterial lysate into a 35 mL polypropylene tube.
Pellet insoluble material in an RC 5B centrifuge at 4°C with an SS-34 rotor at 12,000 rpm for 30 minutes.
Clarify the supernatant using a Stericup 0.45 μm vacuum filter (Millipore).
Measure the protein concentration using the Bradford method.
Ensure the total protein concentration is between 5 to 20 mg/mL.
Aliquot 1 mL of lysate into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Store aliquoted lysate at -80°C.
Determine appropriate conditions for protease cleavage reactions.
Prepare several cleavage reactions with 10-fold dilutions of the protease.
Include control samples such as lysate alone, catalytically inactive mutant of the protease, or pre-inhibited protease.
Setup the cleavage reaction to achieve a final volume of about 1 mL.
Incubate samples with 1 to 10 mg of E. coli lysate in 1x cleavage buffer at 37°C for approximately 15 minutes.
Preincubate protease in 1x cleavage reaction buffer at the temperature used for the cleavage reaction for ~15 minutes.
Add the protease to the _E. coli_ lysate, mix gently by inverting several times, and maintain at the desired temperature for a predetermined time.
Weigh out dry guanidine HCl for a 6M solution, assuming the final volume will be ~1.65 times the cleavage reaction volume.
Add the dry guanidine HCl to the cleavage reaction to stop the reaction.
Add DTT to the reaction mixture to achieve a final concentration of 10 mM.
Vortex well and incubate on a 95°C heat block for 10 minutes.
Cool denatured sample to room temperature.
Alkylate cysteins with 30 mM iodoacetamide in the dark at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Add dry o-methylisourea hemisulfate to guanidinate lysine side chains, achieving a final concentration of 0.5 M.
Adjust the pH to greater or equal to 10.3 with 5 N NaOH.
Incubate at 4°C for ~16 hours.
Prepare an appropriate volume of 9.1 M urea (~500 mL).
Add 2 or 3 large scoops of AG 501-X8 resin to the urea solution, and stir for >=30 minutes.
Clarify urea with a 0.22 μm filter.
Add 1M stock HEPES pH 7.8 to the urea solution to make it 50 mM HEPES and 8 M urea.
Equilibrate PD-10 columns with 25 mL of 8M urea buffer.
Load sample onto PD-10 column, ensuring the volume is <=1.5 mL.
Add 8 M urea buffer to achieve a total volume of 2.5 mL including the sample.
Collect the next 2.5 mL coming off the PD-10 column after loading the sample.
Label N-terminal amines with 5 mM sulfo NHS-SS-biotin for 1 hour at 37 ºC.
Stop reaction by adding 1 M stock AmmBic pH 7.8 to achieve a final concentration of 50 mM.
Reverse ester side reactions with Ser and Thr residues by adding 1 M stock hydroxylamine to reach a final concentration of 40 mM, then incubate at 37 ºC for 15 minutes.
Buffer exchange the sample to 8 M urea buffer using PD-10 columns in two separate runs due to volume exceeding 1.5 mL.
Dilute the sample to 2 M urea with 50 mM AmmBic buffer.
Add 5 to 10 micro g of modified sequence grade trypsin to digest proteins into peptides.
Incubate at 37 ºC overnight for protein digestion.
If any flocculant is visible, spin down the insoluble material at high speed (10,000 rcf) for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Calculate the amount of high capacity neutravidin resin needed for all samples.
Wash the high capacity neutravidin resin with 2 M urea buffer.
Add high capacity neutravidin resin to each sample.
Neutate or rock on a rocker for 30 minutes at 4°C to bind biotinylated peptides.
Load samples on disposable 2 mL polystyrene columns (Pierce).
Wash extensively with 2 M urea buffer 10 times.
Wash with 50 mM AmmBic pH 7.8 buffer 3 times.
Transfer resin to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube in 50 mM AmmBic buffer.
Spin down resin quickly, and remove buffer to the 1 mL marking.
Add 10x TCEP to a final concentration of 5 mM.
Incubate at 37°C with rocking for 30 minutes.
Collect eluted peptides by loading the sample on to MicroBio spin columns and taking the flow through.
Flush the resin with 500 µL of 50 mM AmmBic buffer.
Cleanup peptides using C18 Sep-Pak Vac 6cc cartridges.
Condition the columns with 6 mL of isopropanol, equilibrate with 6 mL of 0.1% TFA, and load samples.
Wash 5 times with 2 mL of 4.25% MeCN, 0.1% TFA.
Elute 5 times with 1 mL of 50% MeCN, 0.1% TFA.
Samples are usually only in the third elution.
Dry samples in a vacuum centrifuge at room temperature.
Solubilize peptides in 40 μL of 2% MeCN, 0.1% TFA.
Store solubilized peptides at 4°C until analysis by LC-MS/MS.
Separate peptides by liquid chromatography prior to MS/MS using reverse phase chromatography.
Load 5-8 μL of sample onto the reverse phase column at 10 μL per minute.
Wash with solvent A (2% MeCN, 0.1% TFA).
Elute over a two-hour linear gradient from 10-60% solvent B (80% MeCN, 0.1% TFA).
Elute directly into the mass spectrometer.
Enable dynamic exclusion to manage highly abundant peptides during MS/MS analysis.
Run each sample 3 or more times to increase non-redundant peptide identifications and improve spectral counts.
Combine MS/MS spectra from repeat runs of the same sample.
Analyze the combined spectra with Sorcerer SEQUEST using specified modifications.
Use a concatenated forward and reverse database to estimate false discovery rate.
Derive the database from the SwissProt proteome database of the pertinent organism.
Use a semi-enzyme database for identifying non-Lys/Arg cleavages.
Annotate N-terminal peptides with N-TerProt software.
Export Peptide Prophet results into Excel spreadsheets.
Add 3 additional columns to each sample dataset: 'sorcerer', 'sample', and 'enzyme'.
Fill the 'sorcerer' column with unique numerical sample identifiers.
Fill the 'sample' column with unique sample descriptions.
Fill the 'enzyme' column with the enzyme used for peptide generation.
Download N-TerProt from the specified website or contact the provided email address.
Save the N-TerProt folder to the designated location on Macintosh HD.
Open the file 'N-TerProt V3.0'.
Run the N-TerProt script and click 'YES' when prompted to run 'Curate Probability & Xcorr'.
Modify parameters by changing the value for the probability score cutoff variable 'probCutOff' or the cross correlation cutoff variable 'xcorrCutoff' if necessary.
Run the N-TerProt script and click 'YES' when prompted to run 'Fix unlabelled N-terminal artifacts'.
Run the N-TerProt script and click 'YES' when prompted to run 'Peptide Stuff'.
Run the N-TerProt script and click 'YES' when prompted to run 'Weird NT & CT Analysis'.
Run the N-TerProt script.
Click 'YES' to run 'NT Index'.
Run the N-TerProt script again.
Click 'YES' to run 'New ES'.
Optional: Run the N-TerProt script one more time.
Click 'YES' to run 'Enzyme & Sample column separation'.
Run the N-TerProt script.

Run the N-TerProt script.

Run the N-TerProt script.

Run the N-TerProt script.

Add new control descriptions to the variable list 'negList' keeping the text in quotes.

Change the variable 'myPosition' in the third line to the desired position keeping the text in quotes.

Clone candidate protease substrates into an amenable expression vector for expression in E. coli.
Express candidate substrates proteins aiming for a concentration of 5 micro M.
Elute proteins in buffer compatible with the cleavage reaction buffer.
Perform the cleavage reaction with protease at a concentration 5-10 fold greater than used in original sample analysis.
Assay protease concentrations using 1/3 dilutions, including substrate alone and maximum protease alone.
Prepare cleavage reaction in Costar 96-well flat bottom microtiter plate in a volume of 100 μL.
Add substrate to appropriate wells, then start the cleavage reaction by adding protease dilution series to respective wells.
Stop the cleavage reaction by adding 50 μL of 3x sample buffer with 30 mM DTT.
Denature on a 95°C heat block for 10 minutes after stopping the reaction.
Load 10-15 μL per lane onto gel for SDS-PAGE visualization.
Stain protein using GelCode Blue or coomassie stain, and destain as directed.
Confirm that the anticipated cleavage products match the banding pattern of the cleavage assay.
If the banding pattern does not match, try increasing the protease concentration as N-terminomics analysis can be more sensitive than SDS-PAGE.
Measure the full-length substrate in all lanes by densitometry to determine the enzyme concentration required for 50% cleavage (E1/2).
Plot the densitometry data to determine the E1/2 value.
Calculate kobs using the equation: _k_obs = ln2 / (_t_ * E1/2).
